quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what happens?

options.text: It makes you feel more confident.

questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your body, it slows your reactions. It also makes you feel too confident and causes you to make more mistakes while driving.

questions.question: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: For drivers age 21 or older, the legal BAC limit is 0.08 percent. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to warn the bicyclist you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane to pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front of them quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists plenty of space. Bicyclists have less protection than car drivers. Do not crowd them, as passing too fast can force them off course.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and watch for hazards.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: The road is most slippery right after rain starts.
Wet roads can cause your car to hydroplane.
You need extra space to stop safely.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are dangerous, especially when rain just starts. Slow down on wet pavement to avoid your wheels losing grip. Remember that your tires slide on a thin layer of water, oil, and dirt.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: What is reasonable and safe for the conditions.
What is safe for the road and traffic conditions.

questions.explanation: You must obey speed limits and drive at a safe speed for the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road condition, and light. Always drive at a speed that is reasonable for the conditions around you.

questions.question: Which statement about wet roads is true?

options.text: Driving faster makes your tires less effective.
Good tires prevent water from affecting your car.
Shallow water is more dangerous than deep water.
Slowing down makes the road more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving faster makes your tires less effective.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on a wet road, the less water your tires can push away. If you go too fast, your tires lose grip and you hydroplane, sliding on the water instead of the road.

questions.question: If your car's right wheels leave the pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Pull all the way off the road and wait.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Let off the gas, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let off the gas, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road.
questions.explanation: Do not panic. Take your foot off the gas and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and use both hands to gently turn the wheel to ease back onto the pavement. Check for traffic before returning to the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers turning left at a green light that they must yield to oncoming traffic. You can turn left when it is safe, even if the light is still green.

questions.question: Compared to daytime driving, nighttime driving is:
questions.explanation: Nighttime driving is more dangerous because visibility is reduced. Other vehicles' headlights can blind you, and there are more tired and impaired drivers on the road at night.

questions.question: You see an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Let the car pass and then pass the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the bicyclist. Do not try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction. Solid white lines cannot be crossed. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: This sign is used to warn drivers:

options.text: That the right lane ends and traffic should merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the right lane ends and traffic should merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the right lane ends ahead. All traffic in the right lane must move to the left lane.

questions.question: On long trips, how can you prevent drowsiness?

options.text: Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.
Moving your eyes from side to side as you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.
questions.explanation: Stop regularly on long trips to rest and stretch. Do this even if you do not feel tired yet.

questions.question: You may drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway:

options.text: As long as you aren't driving.
If you are riding in the back seat.
If you are riding in the back of a pick-up truck.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or carry open alcohol in any vehicle on a public road. This applies to all passengers and all locations in the vehicle.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps ensure safe driving?

options.text: Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking one half hour before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to stay safe is to get a ride from someone who has not been drinking. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol's effects. The body takes about one hour to eliminate one drink.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: No less safe than driving under any other conditions.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers at risk. Stay focused on the road to prevent crashes.

questions.question: As you near an intersection, the traffic light changes from green to yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Apply the brakes sharply to stop.
Be prepared to stop in the center of the intersection.
Be prepared to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Get ready to stop before you enter the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You are entering a crowded freeway. What should you do to merge into traffic?

options.text: Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to adjust your speed to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up and match freeway traffic. Yield to cars already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before you merge.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with opposite traffic, you should:

options.text: Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.
Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, return to the right side when you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: If you get stuck in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Leave the car and walk to get help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. People are more likely to find you there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. People are more likely to find you there.
questions.explanation: If you get stuck in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle. It is also dangerous to walk around outside in a snowstorm.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle in a small car, what should you expect?

options.text: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles. Small car drivers should be ready to steer correctly when passing large vehicles that are moving fast.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through the middle on a sign mean?

options.text: Some drivers must yield to other drivers.

questions.explanation: Some signs tell drivers what they cannot do. These signs are rectangular, white, with red and black symbols. A red circle with a slash over a symbol means that action is forbidden.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns of a steep hill. Slow down to protect your brakes and avoid crashes.

questions.question: What must a driver do at a flashing red traffic light?
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop. Yield to traffic and pedestrians. Go only when it is safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Stop and wait until the lights stop flashing and all warning devices turn off.
